Definition: Motsa, the name of two Israelites
BiblicalUsage: Motsa is the name of two Israelites. One is a son of Zimri in the line of Saul, and the other is a son of Caleb's concubine Ephah, and both are carried in the genealogies so their families are counted.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that two men sharing one name, both counted, is the record's honesty: the lines are kept straight even when the names repeat.
